Let {C_h/Q} be a family of geometrically smooth projective curves of fixed genus g≥2 obtained from a fixed finite list of bounded-degree algebraic schemes over Z[coefficients] by specializing integral parameters of absolute size ≤H, avoiding the finite discriminant locus. Assume for each specialization there is an integral good-reduction denominator/discriminant integer Δ_h≠0 of absolute value ≤H^A (A fixed), such that Jac(C_h) has good reduction outside primes dividing 2Δ_h. Proof: J=Jac C_h, dim g. Set L=Q(J[2]). Its Galois degree ≤|GL_{2g}(F2)|=d_g (constant), and by Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich it is unramified outside rational primes dividing 2Δ_h. In a number field of degree ≤d_g, local discriminant exponents at each ramified rational prime are bounded in terms of d_g (plus bounded adjustment for primes ≤d_g). Thus |Disc(L)|≪(2|Δ_h|)^{A_g}≪H^{O_g(1)}. In fixed degree, Minkowski/standard class-number bounds imply log h_L≪log|Disc L|+1≪log H; also #S_L≪_g 1+log H for S_L=archimedean and primes above 2Δ_h. Over L all J[2] is rational, hence Sel_2(J/L) embeds into the finite-S squareclass group H¹(G_{L,S},J[2])≈(L(S,2))^{2g}, whose F2 dimension ≤2g(|S_fin|+unit rank+dim_F2 Cl(L)[2])=O_g(log H). Therefore rank J(Q)≤rank J(L)≤dim Sel_2(J/L)=O(log H). Apply Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger, Annals of Math. 194(2021), Theorem 1.1 (https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2021/194-1/p04): for g≥2, #C(Q)≤c(g,1)^(1+rank J(Q))≪H^M. If C(Q)=∅ the inequality is immediate. The finite-list genus3/5 FJ norm-lift schemes have bounded coefficients polynomial in |a|,|b|,p ≤p; their nonsingularity, independence, projection and branch-disjointness are certified above by explicit nonzero polynomial discriminants/resultants. Elimination of singular specializations supplies a fixed polynomial Δ(a,b) with 0<|Δ(a,b)|≪p^A at all admissible p (possibly enlarge by finitely many leading coefficients and 2), establishing lemma hypotheses. 2. NEW GLOBAL FINITENESS LEMMA FK.1
For coprime nonzero integers u,v with u²≠v², only finitely many rational ratios u:v can satisfy Kstar = k² for integer k, where a=u²−v², b=2uv. Consequently only finitely many split primes p=u²+v² can produce a square Kstar.


Proof. The identity
Kstar=(a²+b²)²+16a²b²
       =(u²+v²)^4+64u²v²(u²−v²)²
is exact, degree eight. Put t=u/v and Y=k/v⁴. Then every integer-square Kstar yields a Q-point
C: Y²=f(t), f(t)=t⁸+68t⁶−122t⁴+68t²+1.
The octic is squarefree over Q: modulo 3,
f(t)=(t⁴+t³−t+1)(t⁴−t³+t+1),
and gcd_{F3}(f,f')=1 (both quartics occur to exponent 1 and are coprime). Thus its smooth projective normalization is a geometrically integral hyperelliptic curve of genus (8−2)/2=3. By Faltings, C(Q) is finite. A rational t=u/v in lowest terms determines only finitely many primitive signed pairs (u,v), hence only finitely many p=u²+v². QED.
This result is ineffective: it does NOT give a list of the exceptional p, and does not assert that the finite list is empty. The finite examples p=5,13,17,29 have nonsquare Kstar, but samples are not the proof.

Across ALL variable split primes p and distinct split primes q,r, the 52 FJ reducible linear/bilinear Gaussian allocation branches contribute at most O(1) original physical points for R=pqr<=B; implied absolute constant is finite but not explicitly computed.

Summation over the finite exceptional p remains O(1), independent of B. No Gaussian-only virtual points are counted as physical: this is an upper bound on the actual same-P subset of these assignments.
